classification.difficultyReason: Translate each solid into labelled orthographic views, deciding which heights overlap and which face boundaries remain visible. The stepped and recessed solids require coordinating footprint, height and viewing direction using the taught projection method.

content.prompt: Draw the front, side and plan views of the following solids.

spec.description: Single-height bent solid with the original visible edge divisions and two curved viewing arrows.
spec.mathematics: Orthographic projections of a stepped single-level footprint.

answer.short: Front, side and plan views as shown.
answer.worked: Look directly along each labelled arrow for the front and side views. Look vertically down for the plan. Retain visible changes of face.

spec.description: Front rectangle two units wide, side rectangle three units wide with one visible internal division, and stepped plan outline.
spec.mathematics: Three orthographic views matched to teacher evidence.

spec.description: Two-unit-high rectangular block with an attached lower cube; side arrow on the left and front arrow on the right.
spec.mathematics: Occlusion and height differences in orthographic views.

answer.short: Front, side and plan views as shown.
answer.worked: Project the tall block and attached cube along the indicated directions. The plan records their footprint; the elevations retain the lower cube's visible boundary.

spec.description: Square front with lower-right visible square, L-shaped side, and L-shaped plan.
Three-position row with heights one, two and one, with source viewing arrows.
spec.mathematics: A central raised column projects to a T-shaped front.

answer.short: Front, side and plan views as shown.
answer.worked: The front shows column heights $1,2,1$. From the side the columns overlap, giving height 2 and width 1. The plan is a row of three squares.

spec.description: T-shaped front, two-square vertical side and three-square horizontal plan.
Unit-cube wall with consecutive heights 4,1,1,4 and depth one.
spec.mathematics: U-shaped front elevation; depth-one side and plan.

answer.short: Front, side and plan views as shown.
answer.worked: The front retains the four column heights $4,1,1,4$. From the side the columns overlap into one four-cube column. The plan is one row of four squares.

spec.description: Unit-divided U front, vertical four-unit side and horizontal four-unit plan.
Three-level staircase, retaining source proportions without adding dimensions.
spec.mathematics: Constant-width solid staircase with a deeper lowest tread.

answer.short: Front, side and plan views as shown.
answer.worked: The front projects to a rectangle with two horizontal changes of height. The side reveals the three-step profile. The plan shows the three tread regions: the highest and lowest treads have equal depth, and the middle tread is shallower.

spec.description: Source-proportioned staircase elevations and plan; no invented numerical dimensions are printed.
spec.mathematics: Orthographic views of a solid staircase.

spec.description: Raised rear row and lower platform with an open front recess; source edge divisions and arrows retained.
spec.mathematics: A recess affects the plan while the rear row determines the front silhouette.

answer.short: Front, side and plan views as shown.
answer.worked: The raised rear row fills the front silhouette to height 2 across three positions. The side has a two-unit-high rear and a one-unit-high platform. The plan retains the open central recess.

spec.description: Three-by-two divided front, L-shaped side and recessed plan with rear-row boundary.
spec.mathematics: Three views matched to teacher evidence.
